themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked dramatically THIS WEEK to 35 complaints vs. 5.6 weekly average (522% increase, z-score 10.08), coinciding with dead/dying tree complaints jumping to 10 THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 average (700% spike, z-score 9.04), suggesting widespread street deterioration across Park Slope/Carroll Gardens that warrants immediate investigation into root causes and city response.
evidence: Curb Condition complaints: 35 THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly baseline (522% spike, z-score 10.08)
Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 10 THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 9.04)
Combined street/tree crisis suggests coordinated infrastructure failure requiring urgent city response
reporting_angles: Ground canvass of Park Slope and Carroll Gardens to document curb damage and tree conditions; interview affected residents about sidewalk hazards
Obtain NYC Parks and DOT internal reports on tree health assessments and curb repair backlogs in CD 306; interview agency officials on capacity and timeline

themes_detail.label: Traffic and Street Obstruction Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints exploded THIS WEEK to 8 vs. 1.9 weekly average (327% increase, z-score 3.79), paired with obstruction complaints jumping to 14 last week vs. 3.8 average (273% spike, z-score 5.53), suggesting either new construction activity, inadequate traffic management, or encroachment issues that merit urgent investigation.
evidence: Traffic complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (327% increase, z-score 3.79)
Obstruction complaints: 14 last week vs. 3.8 weekly baseline (273% increase, z-score 5.53)
1,237 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (778 alterations) suggest construction activity may be driving congestion
reporting_angles: Map construction sites from DOB data and cross-reference with traffic spike locations; interview DOT on traffic management compliance
Interview residents on specific problem intersections and document via photos/video; check whether construction projects lack proper traffic control plans

themes_detail.label: Vendor and Commercial Enforcement Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked THIS WEEK to 4 vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 4.85), and Commercial Disposal complaints surged last week to 3 vs. 0.4 average (700% spike, z-score 3.77), indicating possible collapse in city enforcement of street vending, food service, and waste disposal rules in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
Commercial Disposal complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 3.77)
Suggests simultaneous enforcement gaps across multiple agencies (DSNY, DOH) in the same district
reporting_angles: Identify which streets/blocks are seeing vendor and disposal violations; canvass those locations and photograph violations for visual evidence
Interview DSNY and DOH enforcement officials on staffing levels, response times, and whether budget cuts or staffing changes have reduced enforcement capacity

themes_detail.label: Gowanus Waterfront Development Momentum
themes_detail.summary: Three active land-use applications in pipeline for Park Slope/Carroll Gardens waterfront area (GSD Waterfront Certification at 444 Carroll, 46 Nelson Street Rezoning in public review, GSD-175 Third Street Certification) alongside completed Gowanus Canal CSO project, signaling significant waterfront redevelopment activity worth tracking for community impact and housing implications.
evidence: 46 Nelson Street Rezoning currently in public review phase (ULURP milestone: Borough President Referral)
GSD Waterfront Certification and GSD-175 Third Street Certification both filed and under agency review
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite need for affordable housing study and land use/zoning review, indicating long-standing resident concerns
reporting_angles: Obtain ULURP application details and community board testimony; interview residents about concerns regarding displacement, gentrification, and affordability
Track relationship between waterfront development, CSO facility completion, and recent infrastructure complaints (curb, tree); interview DCP on long-term neighborhood vision

themes_detail.label: Taxi Complaint Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Taxi complaints spiked to 4 complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 5.21), indicating possible illegal taxi operations, TLC enforcement gaps, or emerging transportation service disruptions in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens warranting follow-up.
evidence: Taxi complaints: 4 complaints (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike, z-score 5.21)
Spike is older than current week but remains statistically anomalous relative to baseline
reporting_angles: Cross-reference TLC data on medallion violations and unlicensed taxi reports in CD 306; interview TLC enforcement officials
Interview residents about nature of taxi complaints (illegal operations, overcharging, safety) to understand what triggered spike
